title: Inside the graphite coating
blurb: A piece of one coating of a negative sheet: copper foil underneath, graphite grains packed on it. The pores between the grains are full of liquid electrolyte; the separator, not drawn, lies on top. Click a grain, then look inside it.
note: To scale: the thickness of the foil (10 µm) and of the coating (76.5 µm), and the size of the grains (10 µm across), all from the parameter set of a measured consumer pouch cell (Ai et al. 2020). Illustrative: the shapes of the grains (real ones are irregular flakes and lumps), their number and their packing; the binder that glues them and the skin on each grain (the SEI, a few nanometres) are not drawn.

labels.text: Graphite grains: lithium is stored inside them
